newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH STATE 98 NET BORROWING SEEN FALLING-PROTOS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH STATE 98 NET BORROWING SEEN FALLING-PROTOS.

text.p: Finnish GDP growth could hit six percent in 1997 and if growth remains strong next year, too, the state's net borrowing requirement could fall below 10 billion markka in 1998, Protos Stockbrokers said on Tuesday.

"According to our calculations, if GDP growth is six percent this year and four to five percent in 1996, the (state's) net borrowing requirement will drop below 10 billion markka in 1998," Protos said in a weekly report.
Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto has said the government will do well if it manages to squeeze 1998 state net borrowing down to 20 billion markka from some 28 billion this year.

Protos said the rapid pace of growth which started in the latter half of 1996 would continue this year with construction expected to expand 15 percent year-on-year in 1997, exports seen growing seven percent and private consumption up four percent.
"Finnish GDP growth could even be as high as six percent this year," it added.
The finance ministry has projected 4.6 percent gowth this year and almost four percent in 1998.
Although growth was brisk, it seemed that the central bank would keep monetary policy on hold for now, Protos said.
"The most recent statements from the Bank of Finland indicate clearly that they are not willing to tighten rates until after the successful completion of the income wage settlement next autumn."
Finnish short-term rates were unlikely to head higher before the autumn, Protos said, adding that there was little upward pressure in the longer rates.
Despite the rapid growth inflation would remain subdued in the near-term.
